title: 7.7 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems, explain what each part stands for, and build one for a situation I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: A town-planning map shows a grid with two corner points of a future rectangular park already marked. The rest of the park is drawn only as a dashed outline waiting for its other two corners.
noticeStarters: I notice the park has two corners marked ___.
I notice the outline still needs a shape ___.
I notice the grid squares stand for distance ___.
wonderStarters: I wonder where the other two corners go ___.
I wonder how far apart two points sit ___.
I wonder what shape this park will become ___.
noticeAndWonder.imageAlt: A town-planning grid with two surveyed park corners marked at negative 4, 3 and 5, negative 3, and the rest of the rectangle drawn as a dashed outline with two unmarked corners.
noticeAndWonder.contextEs: Un mapa de planeación urbana muestra una cuadrícula con dos puntos de esquina de un futuro parque rectangular ya marcados. El resto del parque está dibujado solo como un contorno punteado esperando sus otras dos esquinas.
noticeAndWonder.imageAltEs: Una cuadrícula de planeación urbana con dos esquinas de parque ya medidas y marcadas en menos 4, 3 y en 5, menos 3, y el resto del rectángulo dibujado como un contorno punteado con dos esquinas sin marcar.
noticeStartersEs: Noto que el parque ya tiene dos esquinas marcadas ___.
Noto que el contorno punteado espera su forma ___.
Noto que los cuadros de la cuadrícula representan una distancia ___.
wonderStartersEs: Me pregunto dónde quedarán las otras dos esquinas ___.
Me pregunto qué tan separados están estos dos puntos ___.
Me pregunto qué forma tendrá finalmente este parque ___.

vocabulary.definition: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair on the coordinate plane.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina de un polígono, nombrado por un par ordenado en el plano de coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: The park's corner at (2, 4) — one corner, named by an ordered pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair, is a ___.

examples.text: (5, 4), where two sides of the park meet
examples.why: It is a corner, and a coordinate pair names it.
That is a side; a vertex is the point where sides meet.

vocabulary.definition: A closed figure made of line segments; on the plane you draw it by plotting the vertices and connecting them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cerrada hecha de segmentos; en el plano se dibuja marcando los vértices y conectándolos en orden.
vocabulary.example: Plot the four points, connect them, and the rectangle appears.
vocabulary.visual: Plot (2, 4), (5, 4), (5, −4), (2, −4) and join them — a rectangle appears.
vocabulary.cloze: A closed figure made of line segments is a ___.

examples.text: Four plotted vertices joined in order into a closed rectangle
examples.why: Straight sides, and the figure closes.

examples.text: Three points joined but left open
examples.why: An unclosed path is not a polygon.

vocabulary.definition: The total distance around a polygon — the sum of all its side lengths.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia total alrededor de un polígono: la suma de todos sus lados.
vocabulary.cloze: The total distance around a polygon is its ___.

examples.text: Adding all four side lengths of the rectangle
examples.why: It measures the whole way around.
That gives area — the space inside, not the distance around.

vocabulary.definition: When two vertices share an x- or y-coordinate, the distance between them is the absolute difference of the other coordinates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando dos vértices comparten una coordenada x o y, la distancia es la diferencia absoluta de las otras coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: (2, 4) and (5, 4) share y, so the side is |5 − 2| = 3 units.
vocabulary.cloze: When two vertices share a coordinate, subtract the other and take the ___ ___.

examples.why: Same x, so the side goes up and down. It is 8 units long.
Dropping the − sign makes the side look like 0 units long.

vocabulary.definition: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que representa una unidad de la cuadrícula en la situación real.
vocabulary.example: Each unit is 100 feet, so 3 units of width is 300 feet.
vocabulary.visual: Each grid unit = 100 feet, so 8 units of map is 800 real feet.
vocabulary.cloze: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation is the ___.

examples.text: 1 unit = 100 feet on the park map
examples.why: It converts grid units into real distance.

examples.text: The number of units between two vertices
examples.why: That is a length on the grid; the scale is what a unit means.

vocabulary.definition: The distance between two vertices that are joined by a side.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia entre dos vértices unidos por un lado.
vocabulary.visual: Found with absolute value when the points share a coordinate.
vocabulary.cloze: The distance between two joined vertices is a ___.

examples.why: |−4.25| + |3.5| = 7.75 is the distance along the side.
A coordinate is a position, not a distance.

turnAndTalk.question: The vertices (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3, so the side between them is horizontal, with length |5 − (−4.5)| = 9.5. Why is that side's length found by comparing the x-coordinates instead of the y-coordinates?
turnAndTalk.kernel: When two vertices share the same y-coordinate, the segment between them is horizontal, so its length comes from the DIFFERENCE in the coordinate that changes — the x-coordinates.

stems.en: The side is horizontal because both vertices share the same ___-coordinate.
stems.es: El lado es horizontal porque ambos vértices comparten la misma coordenada ___.

stems.en: I subtract the ___-coordinates because that's the coordinate that ___.
stems.es: Resto las coordenadas ___ porque esa es la coordenada que ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Vertices (5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5 instead. Justify why the distance between them is |3 − (−3.75)| = 6.75 and not just 3.75 − 3.
extendStems: The distance is 6.75, not 0.75, because the segment crosses ___, so you add the distance from 3 to 0 and from 0 to ___.
Using absolute value matters here because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: You sorted pairs of vertices into 'subtract coordinates' versus 'slanted.' How did you decide that (0, 0) and (4, 3) belonged in the slanted group?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Coordinates can be subtracted directly only when two vertices share an x-value or a y-value; if BOTH coordinates differ, the segment is slanted and this lesson's subtraction method doesn't apply.

stems.en: (0, 0) and (4, 3) are slanted because they don't share the same ___ or the same ___.
stems.es: (0, 0) y (4, 3) están inclinados porque no comparten la misma ___ ni la misma ___.

stems.en: (-4, 1) and (6, 1) belong with 'subtract coordinates' because they share ___.
stems.es: (-4, 1) y (6, 1) van con 'restar coordenadas' porque comparten ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Explain why a rectangle drawn from four vertices will always have sides you CAN find by subtracting coordinates, even though a slanted pair exists elsewhere on the same grid.
extendStems: A rectangle's sides always share a coordinate because ___.
The diagonal of the rectangle would be slanted because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The Town Square park's two known vertices are 3 units apart, and each unit represents 100 feet, so the width is 300 feet. The park's area must be 240,000 square feet. How do you use that to find how many units below the known vertices the missing vertices go?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Length = area ÷ width gives 800 feet, and dividing that by the 100-feet-per-unit scale converts it to 8 map units.

stems.en: Converting to map units, I divide ___ feet by ___ to get ___ units.
stems.es: Al convertir a unidades del mapa, divido ___ pies entre ___ para obtener ___ unidades.

turnAndTalk.extend: Explain why dividing by 100 (the scale) is necessary at the end, instead of just using the 800 feet directly as the number of units to move on the grid.
extendStems: The scale tells us that one grid unit equals ___ feet, so we must ___ before placing the new vertices.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a problem where you found the perimeter of a rectangle from its vertices. What were your steps from the coordinates to the final perimeter?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Finding a rectangle's perimeter from vertices means finding two different side lengths using coordinate subtraction, then computing 2(length) + 2(width).

stems.en: First I found the width using vertices ___ and ___, which gave ___ units.
stems.es: Primero encontré el ancho usando los vértices ___ y ___, lo cual dio ___ unidades.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate computed the perimeter of a rectangle with sides 9.5 and 6.75 as 9.5 × 6.75 = 64.125. What did they compute instead, and how would you help them fix it?
extendStems: They computed the ___ of the rectangle instead of the perimeter.
I would tell them perimeter means adding around the outside, so it should be 2(___) + 2(___) instead of multiplying.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 7.7. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane
conceptIntro.intro: Use the coordinates you know to find a missing vertex. Then use the side lengths to find area.
conceptIntro.introEs: Usa las coordenadas que conoces para hallar un vértice que falta. Luego usa las longitudes de los lados para hallar el área.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Coordinates give exact side lengths, so you can find a missing vertex, the perimeter, and the area without measuring.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Las coordenadas dan las longitudes exactas de los lados, así que puedes hallar un vértice que falta, el perímetro y el área sin medir.

iDo.title: Example · Missing vertex and area
iDo.titleEs: Ejemplo · Vértice que falta y área
lines: Three vertices of a rectangle are (−2, 3), (4, 3) and (4, −1). Find the fourth vertex. Then find the area.
Find the length of the side across: (−2, 3) to (4, 3) → 2 + 4 = 6
Find the length of the side up and down: (4, 3) to (4, −1) → 3 + 1 = 4
Multiply length by width for the area: 6 × 4 = 24
The fourth vertex is (−2, −1). The area is 24 square units.
linesEs: Tres vértices de un rectángulo son (−2, 3), (4, 3) y (4, −1). Halla el cuarto vértice. Luego halla el área.
Halla la longitud del lado horizontal: (−2, 3) a (4, 3) → 2 + 4 = 6
Halla la longitud del lado vertical: (4, 3) a (4, −1) → 3 + 1 = 4
Multiplica el largo por el ancho para hallar el área: 6 × 4 = 24
El cuarto vértice es (−2, −1). El área es de 24 unidades cuadradas.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: The rectangle with vertices (−4.5, 3), (5, 3), (5, −3.75) and (−4.5, −3.75) has sides of 9.5 and 6.75 units. Find its perimeter.
How many sides have each length? (Two sides of 9.5 and two sides of 6.75.)
Why is 9.5 × 6.75 not the perimeter? (9.5 × 6.75 is the area, the space inside. Perimeter is the distance around.)
linesEs: El rectángulo con vértices (−4.5, 3), (5, 3), (5, −3.75) y (−4.5, −3.75) tiene lados de 9.5 y 6.75 unidades. Halla su perímetro.
¿Cuántos lados tienen cada longitud? (Dos lados de 9.5 y dos lados de 6.75.)
¿Por qué 9.5 × 6.75 no es el perímetro? (9.5 × 6.75 es el área, el espacio de adentro. El perímetro es la distancia alrededor.)

youDo.title: Your turn
lines: A square has vertices (−1, 2), (3, 2), (3, −2) and (−1, −2). Each grid unit is 10 feet. What is the perimeter in feet?
Why can you multiply one side by 4 for this shape?
linesEs: Un cuadrado tiene vértices (−1, 2), (3, 2), (3, −2) y (−1, −2). Cada unidad de la cuadrícula mide 10 pies. ¿Cuál es el perímetro en pies?
¿Por qué puedes multiplicar un lado por 4 en esta figura?

build.todayIdea: Use the coordinates you know to find a missing vertex. Then use the side lengths to find area.
build.todayIdeaEs: Usa las coordenadas que conoces para hallar un vértice que falta. Luego usa las longitudes de los lados para hallar el área.

examples.title: Example · Missing vertex and area
examples.titleEs: Ejemplo · Vértice que falta y área
examples.problem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (−2, 3), (4, 3) and (4, −1). Find the fourth vertex. Then find the area.
examples.problemEs: Tres vértices de un rectángulo son (−2, 3), (4, 3) y (4, −1). Halla el cuarto vértice. Luego halla el área.

figure.caption: The fourth vertex closes the rectangle.
figure.captionEs: El cuarto vértice cierra el rectángulo.

steps.do: Find the length of the side across.
steps.doEs: Halla la longitud del lado horizontal.
steps.why: −2 and 4 are on opposite sides of 0, so add |−2| and |4|.
steps.whyEs: −2 y 4 están en lados opuestos del 0, así que suma |−2| y |4|.

steps.do: Find the length of the side up and down.
steps.doEs: Halla la longitud del lado vertical.

steps.why: It shares x with (−2, 3) and y with (4, −1).
steps.whyEs: Comparte la x con (−2, 3) y la y con (4, −1).

steps.do: Multiply length by width for the area.
steps.doEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho para hallar el área.

examples.answer: The fourth vertex is (−2, −1). The area is 24 square units.
examples.answerEs: El cuarto vértice es (−2, −1). El área es de 24 unidades cuadradas.

together.title: Try it together — then prove it
together.problem: The rectangle with vertices (−4.5, 3), (5, 3), (5, −3.75) and (−4.5, −3.75) has sides of 9.5 and 6.75 units. Find its perimeter.
together.problemEs: El rectángulo con vértices (−4.5, 3), (5, 3), (5, −3.75) y (−4.5, −3.75) tiene lados de 9.5 y 6.75 unidades. Halla su perímetro.

steps.ask: How many sides have each length?
steps.answer: Two sides of 9.5 and two sides of 6.75.
steps.answerEs: Dos lados de 9.5 y dos lados de 6.75.

steps.answer: 9.5 × 6.75 is the area, the space inside. Perimeter is the distance around.
steps.answerEs: 9.5 × 6.75 es el área, el espacio de adentro. El perímetro es la distancia alrededor.

tryIt.problem: A square has vertices (−1, 2), (3, 2), (3, −2) and (−1, −2). Each grid unit is 10 feet. What is the perimeter in feet?
tryIt.problemEs: Un cuadrado tiene vértices (−1, 2), (3, 2), (3, −2) y (−1, −2). Cada unidad de la cuadrícula mide 10 pies. ¿Cuál es el perímetro en pies?
tryIt.hint: Find one side in grid units. Then change units to feet.
tryIt.hintEs: Halla un lado en unidades de la cuadrícula. Luego cambia las unidades a pies.
tryIt.explain: Why can you multiply one side by 4 for this shape?
tryIt.explainEs: ¿Por qué puedes multiplicar un lado por 4 en esta figura?
tryIt.modelExplanation: It is a square, so all four sides are equal. One side is 1 + 3 = 4 units, and 4 × 10 = 40 feet. The perimeter is 4 × 40 = 160 feet.
tryIt.modelExplanationEs: Es un cuadrado, así que los cuatro lados son iguales. Un lado mide 1 + 3 = 4 unidades, y 4 × 10 = 40 pies. El perímetro es 4 × 40 = 160 pies.

build.bigIdea: Coordinates give exact side lengths, so you can find a missing vertex, the perimeter, and the area without measuring.
build.bigIdeaEs: Las coordenadas dan las longitudes exactas de los lados, así que puedes hallar un vértice que falta, el perímetro y el área sin medir.

together.problem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (−5, −1), (2, −1) and (2, 4). Find the fourth vertex. Then find the area.
together.problemEs: Tres vértices de un rectángulo son (−5, −1), (2, −1) y (2, 4). Halla el cuarto vértice. Luego halla el área.

steps.answer: (−5, 4). It shares x with (−5, −1) and y with (2, 4).
steps.answerEs: (−5, 4). Comparte la x con (−5, −1) y la y con (2, 4).

steps.askEs: Halla las dos longitudes de los lados.

together.answer: The fourth vertex is (−5, 4). The area is 7 × 5 = 35 square units.
together.answerEs: El cuarto vértice es (−5, 4). El área es 7 × 5 = 35 unidades cuadradas.

together.problem: A park on a map has vertices (−2, 3), (4, 3), (4, −1) and (−2, −1). Each unit is 50 feet. What is the perimeter in feet?
together.problemEs: Un parque en un mapa tiene vértices (−2, 3), (4, 3), (4, −1) y (−2, −1). Cada unidad es 50 pies. ¿Cuál es el perímetro en pies?

steps.ask: Find the two side lengths in units.
steps.askEs: Halla las dos longitudes en unidades.

steps.ask: Each unit is 50 feet. What is the perimeter in feet?
steps.askEs: Cada unidad es 50 pies. ¿Cuál es el perímetro en pies?

steps.ask: Why is the side from (4, 3) to (4, −1) 4 units, not 2?
steps.askEs: ¿Por qué el lado de (4, 3) a (4, −1) mide 4 unidades y no 2?
steps.answer: The points are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so we add 3 + 1 = 4.
steps.answerEs: Los puntos están en lados opuestos del eje x, así que sumamos 3 + 1 = 4.

together.answer: The perimeter is 20 units, or 20 × 50 = 1,000 feet.
together.answerEs: El perímetro es 20 unidades, o 20 × 50 = 1,000 pies.

onMyOwn.problem: A rectangle has vertices (−6, 2), (−1, 2) and (−1, −3). The fourth vertex is (−6, ?). What is the missing y-coordinate?
onMyOwn.problemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (−6, 2), (−1, 2) y (−1, −3). El cuarto vértice es (−6, ?). ¿Cuál es la coordenada y que falta?
onMyOwn.hint: The fourth vertex is on the same horizontal line as (−1, −3).
onMyOwn.hintEs: El cuarto vértice está en la misma línea horizontal que (−1, −3).

onMyOwn.problem: The top side of a rectangle goes from (−3, 4) to (5, 4). The area is 48 square units. What is the y-coordinate of the bottom side?
onMyOwn.problemEs: El lado de arriba de un rectángulo va de (−3, 4) a (5, 4). El área es 48 unidades cuadradas. ¿Cuál es la coordenada y del lado de abajo?
onMyOwn.hint: Find the length of the top side. Then use the area to find the height.
onMyOwn.hintEs: Halla la longitud del lado de arriba. Luego usa el área para hallar la altura.
onMyOwn.explain: How did you use the area to find the bottom side?
onMyOwn.explainEs: ¿Cómo usaste el área para hallar el lado de abajo?
onMyOwn.modelExplanation: The top side is 3 + 5 = 8 units. 48 ÷ 8 = 6, so the height is 6. The bottom side is 6 units down from y = 4, and 4 − 6 = −2.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: El lado de arriba mide 3 + 5 = 8 unidades. 48 ÷ 8 = 6, así que la altura es 6. El lado de abajo está 6 unidades más abajo de y = 4, y 4 − 6 = −2.

onMyOwn.problem: A store space is a rectangle with corners (0, 0), (24, 0), (24, 15) and (0, 15). Each unit is 1 foot. Rent is $2 per square foot each month. What is the monthly rent?
onMyOwn.problemEs: Un local es un rectángulo con esquinas (0, 0), (24, 0), (24, 15) y (0, 15). Cada unidad es 1 pie. La renta es $2 por pie cuadrado al mes. ¿Cuál es la renta mensual?
onMyOwn.hint: Find the area in square feet first. Then multiply by the rent for each square foot.
onMyOwn.hintEs: Primero halla el área en pies cuadrados. Luego multiplica por la renta de cada pie cuadrado.

onMyOwn.problem: Space A has corners (0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20) and (0, 20). Space B has corners (0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 12) and (0, 12). Each unit is 1 foot. Which space has more floor area?
onMyOwn.problemEs: El espacio A tiene esquinas (0, 0), (20, 0), (20, 20) y (0, 20). El espacio B tiene esquinas (0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 12) y (0, 12). Cada unidad es 1 pie. ¿Qué espacio tiene más área de piso?
choiceWhy: Space B has a longer side, but its area is 30 × 12 = 360. That is less than 20 × 20 = 400.
Find each area: 20 × 20 = 400 and 30 × 12 = 360. They are not equal.
choiceWhyEs: El espacio B tiene un lado más largo, pero su área es 30 × 12 = 360, menos que 20 × 20 = 400.
Halla cada área: 20 × 20 = 400 y 30 × 12 = 360. No son iguales.
onMyOwn.hint: Find the length and width of each space. Then find each area.
onMyOwn.hintEs: Halla el largo y el ancho de cada espacio. Luego halla cada área.

steps.do: Find the area of Space A.
steps.doEs: Halla el área del espacio A.

steps.do: Find the area of Space B.
steps.doEs: Halla el área del espacio B.

onMyOwn.explain: Why can the longer space have less area?
onMyOwn.explainEs: ¿Por qué el espacio más largo puede tener menos área?
onMyOwn.modelExplanation: Area uses both sides. Space B is longer, but it is much narrower. 30 × 12 = 360 is less than 20 × 20 = 400.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: El área usa los dos lados. El espacio B es más largo, pero es mucho más angosto. 30 × 12 = 360 es menos que 20 × 20 = 400.

talk.prompt: Space B is longer than Space A, but Space A has more area. How can that be? Use the side lengths to explain.
talk.promptEs: El espacio B es más largo que el espacio A, pero el espacio A tiene más área. ¿Cómo puede ser? Usa las longitudes de los lados para explicar.
frames: Space A has more area because ___.
A longer side does not always mean more area because ___.
framesEs: El espacio A tiene más área porque ___.
Un lado más largo no siempre quiere decir más área porque ___.

check.problem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (−4, 2), (4, 2) and (4, −3). What is the area of the rectangle?
check.problemEs: Tres vértices de un rectángulo son (−4, 2), (4, 2) y (4, −3). ¿Cuál es el área del rectángulo?
check.hint: You do not need the fourth vertex to find the two side lengths.
check.hintEs: No necesitas el cuarto vértice para hallar las dos longitudes.

steps.doEs: Halla el lado de lado a lado.

steps.do: Find the side up and down.
steps.doEs: Halla el lado de arriba abajo.

check.problem: A school draws its playground on a grid. The corners are (−20, 10), (25, 10), (25, −10) and (−20, −10). Each unit is 1 meter. How many meters of fence go all the way around?
check.problemEs: Una escuela dibuja su patio en una cuadrícula. Las esquinas son (−20, 10), (25, 10), (25, −10) y (−20, −10). Cada unidad es 1 metro. ¿Cuántos metros de cerca rodean todo el patio?
check.hint: A fence all the way around is the perimeter. Each side crosses an axis.
check.hintEs: Una cerca alrededor de todo es el perímetro. Cada lado cruza un eje.

stretch.problem: A polygon has vertices (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, 0), (5, 0), (5, −2) and (−4, −2). Find its area.
stretch.problemEs: Un polígono tiene vértices (−4, 3), (2, 3), (2, 0), (5, 0), (5, −2) y (−4, −2). Halla su área.

figure.caption: An L-shape. Split it into two rectangles.
figure.captionEs: Una figura en L. Divídela en dos rectángulos.

stretch.hint: Cut the shape along the x-axis. Find the area of each rectangle.
stretch.hintEs: Corta la figura por el eje x. Halla el área de cada rectángulo.

explore.label: Sort each pair of vertices: can you find the distance between them by SUBTRACTING COORDINATES, or would the segment be slanted (not this lesson's tool)?
categories: Same x or same y — subtract coordinates
Slanted — coordinates alone won't give it yet
explore.instructions: Go deeper: Sort all eight, then pick one 'subtract' pair and say the distance out loud with its absolute-value sentence. As you work, ask yourself why it works.

diagram.title: Plot the Park Rectangle
diagram.caption: P and Q share y = 1, so PQ = |6 - (-4)| = 10 units. Q and R share x = 6, so QR = |1 - (-3)| = 4 units. Perimeter = 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 units.
diagram.captionEs: P y Q comparten y = 1, así que PQ = |6 - (-4)| = 10 unidades. Q y R comparten x = 6, así que QR = |1 - (-3)| = 4 unidades. Perímetro = 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 unidades.

explore.instructionsEs: Ve más a fondo: Clasifica las ocho y luego escoge un par de «restar» y di la distancia en voz alta con su oración de valor absoluto. Mientras trabajas, pregúntate por qué funciona.
explore.labelEs: Clasifica cada par de vértices: ¿puedes hallar la distancia entre ellos restando coordenadas, o el segmento quedaría inclinado (que no es la herramienta de esta lección)?

connect.scenario: Designing the Town Square: a rectangular park will have an area of 240,000 square feet. Two vertices are already marked on the planning grid, 3 units apart, and each grid unit represents 100 feet.
connect.promptQuestion: Where do the other two vertices go — and how do the known coordinates, the scale, and the area work together to tell you?
connect.prompt: The park's width is ___ feet. Using the area formula, its length is ___ feet, which is ___ units on the map — so the new vertices sit that many units below the known ones.

check.stem: The two known vertices of the park are 3 units apart, and each grid unit represents 100 feet. What is the park's width in feet?
check.explanation: Multiply the unit distance by the scale: 3 units × 100 feet per unit = 300 feet. Leaving off the scale (3 feet) or adding instead of multiplying (103 feet) ignores what the scale means.
check.stemEs: Los dos vértices conocidos del parque están a 3 unidades de distancia, y cada unidad de la cuadrícula representa 100 pies. ¿Cuál es el ancho del parque en pies?
check.explanationEs: Multiplica la distancia unitaria por la escala: 3 unidades × 100 pies por unidad = 300 pies. Dejar fuera la escala (3 pies) o sumar en vez de multiplicar (103 pies) ignora lo que significa la escala.

check.stem: The park's area must be 240,000 sq ft and its width is 300 ft. What is its length?
check.explanation: Length = area ÷ width = 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 feet. Adding the width to the area (240,300) confuses two different operations — area and length combine here by division, not addition.
check.stemEs: El área del parque debe ser 240,000 pies cuadrados y su ancho es 300 pies. ¿Cuál es su largo?
check.explanationEs: Largo = área ÷ ancho = 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 pies. Sumarle el ancho al área (240,300) confunde dos operaciones distintas — aquí el área y el largo se combinan dividiendo, no sumando.

check.stem: The park's length is 800 feet, and each grid unit represents 100 feet. How many units below the known vertices do the new corners sit?
check.explanation: Convert feet back to units by dividing by the scale: 800 ÷ 100 = 8 units. Dividing by 10 instead of 100 gives 80, and skipping the conversion entirely leaves the answer in feet (800), not map units.
check.stemEs: El largo del parque es 800 pies, y cada unidad de la cuadrícula representa 100 pies. ¿Cuántas unidades debajo de los vértices conocidos quedan las esquinas nuevas?
check.explanationEs: Convierte los pies de regreso a unidades dividiendo entre la escala: 800 ÷ 100 = 8 unidades. Dividir entre 10 da 80, y saltarse la conversión deja la respuesta en pies (800), no en unidades del mapa.

connect.modelAnswer: The marked vertices are 3 units apart, and each unit is 100 feet, so the width is 300 feet. The area must be 240,000 square feet, so the length is 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 feet. Dividing by the scale, 800 ÷ 100 = 8 units, so the other two vertices go 8 units below the known vertices.
connect.promptEs: El ancho del parque es ___ pies. Usando la fórmula del área, su largo es ___ pies, que son ___ unidades en el mapa — así que los vértices nuevos quedan esa cantidad de unidades debajo de los conocidos.
connect.scenarioEs: Diseñando la plaza del pueblo: un parque rectangular tendrá un área de 240,000 pies cuadrados. Dos vértices ya están marcados en la cuadrícula de planeación, a 3 unidades de distancia, y cada unidad de la cuadrícula representa 100 pies.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿A dónde van los otros dos vértices — y cómo trabajan juntas las coordenadas conocidas, la escala y el área para decírtelo?
connect.modelAnswerEs: Los vértices marcados están a 3 unidades de distancia, y cada unidad son 100 pies, así que el ancho es 300 pies. El área debe ser 240,000 pies cuadrados, así que el largo es 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 pies. Dividiendo entre la escala, 800 ÷ 100 = 8 unidades, así que los otros dos vértices van 8 unidades debajo de los vértices conocidos.

diagram.caption: The two horizontal sides are each |4 − (−3)| = 7 units and the two vertical sides are each |2 − (−1)| = 3 units, so the perimeter is 7 + 7 + 3 + 3 = 20 units.

hintsEs: La distancia que cruza el cero suma las dos distancias desde el eje: de −4 a 5 es 4 + 5.

extending.explanation: From (−4, 3) to (5, 3): the x-values sit on opposite sides of zero, so the distance is 4 + 5 = 9. From (5, 3) to (5, −4): 3 + 4 = 7. From (−2, −1) to (6, −1): 2 + 6 = 8. Coordinates turn side lengths into arithmetic — no ruler required.
extending.explanationEs: De (−4, 3) a (5, 3): los valores de x están en lados opuestos del cero, así que la distancia es 4 + 5 = 9. De (5, 3) a (5, −4): 3 + 4 = 7. De (−2, −1) a (6, −1): 2 + 6 = 8. Las coordenadas convierten las longitudes en aritmética: no hace falta regla.

extending.labelEs: Ubica los vértices del rectángulo PQRS y luego usa las coordenadas para hallar su perímetro.
hints: Move right for x first, then up for y — every vertex starts at the origin.

hintsEs: Muévete a la derecha para x primero y luego hacia arriba para y: cada vértice empieza en el origen.
Después de ubicar, resta coordenadas: PQ comparte y = 2, así que su longitud es 6 − 1 = 5.
extending.explanation: P and Q share y = 2, so PQ = 6 − 1 = 5 units; Q and R share x = 6, so QR = 5 − 2 = 3 units. The rectangle is 5 by 3, giving perimeter 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 units and area 5 × 3 = 15 square units — all read straight off the coordinates.
extending.explanationEs: P y Q comparten y = 2, así que PQ = 6 − 1 = 5 unidades; Q y R comparten x = 6, así que QR = 5 − 2 = 3 unidades. El rectángulo mide 5 por 3, con perímetro 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 unidades y área 5 × 3 = 15 unidades cuadradas: todo se lee directo de las coordenadas.

extending.stem: A rectangle has vertices (a, b), (a + w, b), (a + w, b + h), and (a, b + h). Write expressions for its side lengths, perimeter, and area that work for ANY a, b, w, and h. Then explain why a and b never appear in your perimeter or area.
extending.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (a, b), (a + w, b), (a + w, b + h) y (a, b + h). Escribe expresiones para sus lados, su perímetro y su área que sirvan para CUALQUIER a, b, w y h. Después explica por qué a y b nunca aparecen en tu perímetro ni en tu área.
extending.modelAnswer: Horizontal side: |(a + w) − a| = w. Vertical side: |(b + h) − b| = h. Perimeter = 2(w + h), area = w · h. The a and b subtract away, because a side length is a DIFFERENCE of coordinates and both endpoints carry the same a (or the same b). That is the whole reason they vanish: a and b say where the rectangle sits, not how big it is. Slide it anywhere on the plane and w and h are untouched, so the perimeter and area cannot change.
extending.modelAnswerEs: Lado horizontal: |(a + w) − a| = w. Lado vertical: |(b + h) − b| = h. Perímetro = 2(w + h), área = w · h. La a y la b se restan y desaparecen, porque la longitud de un lado es una DIFERENCIA de coordenadas y los dos extremos llevan la misma a (o la misma b). Esa es toda la razón: a y b dicen dónde está el rectángulo, no qué tan grande es. Deslízalo a cualquier lugar del plano y w y h no cambian, así que el perímetro y el área tampoco pueden cambiar.

practice.commonMistake: Subtracting coordinates without the absolute value — from y = 3 down to y = −3.75 the distance is 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units, not 3.75 − 3 = 0.75. Distances that cross zero are the whole reason the absolute value is there.

topic: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Maria's Craft Store
revealWordProblem.text:
Maria, a craft store owner, plans to rent a location in a shopping center and is considering the two spaces shown on the grid. Each unit represents one foot, so each line on the grid represents 5 feet. Space A rents for $13.89 per square foot each month, and Space B rents for $13.49 per square foot each month. Maria wants to pay the lower total monthly rent.
Question: Which location would you recommend she rent?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two shop spaces drawn as polygons on a coordinate grid, labeled Space A and Space B, with vertices at 0 comma 0, 5 comma 35, 15 comma 35, 15 comma 0, and 39 comma 0.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Space A is a trapezoid with parallel horizontal bases 15 feet and 15 − 5 = 10 feet, and height 35 feet. Its area is ½ × (15 + 10) × 35 = 437.5 square feet. Space B is a triangle with base 39 − 15 = 24 feet and height 35 feet, so its area is ½ × 24 × 35 = 420 square feet. Space A costs 437.5 × $13.89 = $6,076.875, or $6,076.88 per month to the nearest cent. Space B costs 420 × $13.49 = $5,665.80 per month. Recommend Space B for the lower total monthly rent. It saves about $411.08 per month while providing 17.5 fewer square feet.
